purpose: Show that myocarditis risk is rare and concentrated by sex, dose and product while keeping two incompatible denominators and scales visibly separate.
title: Myocarditis risk is concentrated rather than uniform
subtitle: Two datasets · compare within each panel only · whiskers are 95% confidence intervals
story: Pooled adolescent cases per million vaccine doses were higher in males than females and after dose 2 than dose 1.
Among Nordic males aged 16–24, excess cases per million vaccinated after dose 2 were higher for mRNA-1273 than BNT162b2.
Panel A reports observed pooled rates; panel B reports excess events above estimated background, so bar lengths must not be compared across panels.

panel_b.denominator: excess cases per million vaccinated after dose 2

layout_notes: Use two clean side-by-side panels labelled a and b with independent black axes and tick marks.
Use dot-and-whisker marks rather than bars; direct-label each estimate in black.
Use only thin keylines between panels; no background gridlines, panel cards, heart illustration, shield, or warning icon.
Place denominator definitions in a compact black-text key below the panels.
constraints: Panel A must use a 0–120 linear axis and panel B a separate 0–300 linear axis.
Every dot and confidence interval endpoint must be proportional to the supplied axis.
Sex and dose are separate pooled subgroup analyses, not a crossed comparison.
The cross-panel comparison warning must be prominent but typographically restrained.
exact_text: Myocarditis risk is concentrated, not uniform
Two datasets · compare within each panel only · whiskers are 95% confidence intervals
Sex and dose are separate pooled subgroup analyses
Excess cases per million vaccinated after dose 2
Do not compare magnitudes across panels
Panel a = observed cases per million vaccine doses
Panel b = excess cases per million vaccinated people
